title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers used AI-generated videos and fake social media profiles to impersonate a real immigration attorney and solicit payments from immigrants for legal services never provided. The deployment failure was on social media platforms, where hundreds of impersonation accounts operated across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram before removal. Catching this would have required social media platforms to verify the identity of accounts offering legal services, or to flag AI-generated video content, before these accounts accumulated thousands of fake testimonials and directed victims to payment services.

This is impersonation enabled by synthetic media rather than a failure of an AI system's training or reasoning. The scammers weaponized AI video generation to make their false claims more convincing, but the core fraud was identity theft and theft of services. It is not established how many people paid or how much was lost beyond one reported case of a legal resident losing thousands of dollars.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an elaborate AI-powered scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos depicting Leal offering immigration services he never provided, including US residency assistance for $2,200. The fraud has escalated dramatically over the past three months, with scammers directing potential victims through WhatsApp to request payment via digital money transfer services like Venmo and Zelle. Leal's office discovered the scheme when clients began calling about services advertised on social media.

After hiring an online anti-piracy company, Leal's team has removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams often feature fake testimonials from supposed former clients praising Leal's work. Leal plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to launch an investigation. He is warning immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to be cautious of social media advertisements, noting that his legitimate office never requests payment over the phone.
